newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG FAIL TO GET MUCH-NEEDED VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG FAIL TO GET MUCH-NEEDED VICTORY.

text.p: Midfielder Cedric Daury scored a shock equaliser as Cannes held crisis-ridden Paris St Germain 1-1 in the French first division at the Parc des Princes on Saturday.
PSG, who have not recorded a home win since November, remain six points adrift of leaders Monaco, who beat them 2-0 last weekend and will pull nine clear if they win at Lyon on Sunday.

Champions Auxerre climbed from seventh to fourth behind Bastia, who are at home to Strasbourg on Sunday, and 10 points behind Monaco after striker Lilian Laslandes scored in injury time to give them a 1-0 home win over Nancy.
"The main thing is that we got the three points and are back among the leaders," Laslandes said.
Saturday was the lowest scoring day of the championship so far with nine goals in eight games.

Caen had defender Stephane Moreau sent off nine minutes from time for violent play at Rennes, who kept their unbeaten home record in a 1-1 draw with a 66th-minute equaliser by Laurent Huard. Macedonian Alen Bajkusa put Caen ahead in the 12th.

At the Parc des Princes, PSG made am excellent start when striker Cyrille Pouget scored his first league goal for his new club to put them ahead in the 12th minute, volleying home a cross from Portuguese defender Kenedy.

But after half an hour PSG lost centre-back Alain Roche when he aggravated a knee injury in his first match back from a long layoff and coach Ricardo was obliged to reshuffle a defence with only one recognised central defender available. Bruno N'Gotty is also injured.
Four minutes into the second half, Jean-Jacques Etame, who had a goal disallowed for handball before the interval, launched an attack with a big kick ahead from deep in the Cannes half.

Fellow midfielder Cedric Daury chased the kick, had his first shot blocked on the edge of the box by PSG keeper Bernard Lama but knocked the ball home when it came back from the right to give the visitors a shock equaliser.
PSG camped in the Cannes half for the remainder of the match but failed to put a much needed winning goal past a packed defence despite a string of chances.
Their Brazilian captain Rai said: "We showed some progress, but the result and the finishing were not there.
"After the equaliser we pressed them and did all we could to win. We must keep at it and when the win comes it will bring back the confidence."
Guinean striker Aboubacar Camara scored twice as early season leaders Lens beat Guingamp 2-1 at home to end a nine-match streak without victory and climb one place to 15th.
Nantes stretched their unbeaten run in the league to 18 games with a 1-0 win at Metz. Midfielder Jocelyn Gourvenec scored one minute after the interval.
Fifth-placed Bordeaux's match at Lille kicked off nearly 20 minutes late because of a floodlighting failure. It ended 0-0.
